Jalgham Abuazuom Emhemmed Ali
Department of African Languages and Studies, Faculty of Languages, Sebha University, Libya
Keywords: Novel, Written Literature, Technical Techniques, Style, Literature

A B S T R A C T
A work of literature, including a novel, is formed by technique and content, which together constitute what we refer to as literature. Technique is composed of elements such as characters, style, setting, structure, and the use of language. These elements are utilized by writers in various ways depending on their skills and abilities. In terms of technique, it refers to the overall main ideas expressed by the author or narrator of the literary work and intended for the audience to receive. This work was intended to investigate the various themes presented by Mohamed Suleiman in his Swahili novel "Kiu." Through this novel, we have identified and discussed the literary techniques used by the author to bring out the themes within the novel. 'Kiu' is a Swahili novel that tells the story of Bahati, a young woman who was raised with care and is now encountering Idi, a deceitful man. Idi quickly entangles Bahati in the trap of false love. While Bahati is deeply immersed in love, unaware of herself and her surroundings, she realizes that Idi does not truly love her, but instead loves only himself, and that she, Bahati, is merely an instrument to fulfill his worldly desires. Like a bird caught in a snare, her efforts to find escape only lead her closer to ruin. Introduction

3. The Swahili novel is one of the four genres of written Swahili literature, the others being drama, poetry, and the short story (Wamitila, 2008). The novel genre is used to explain matters in greater depth and breadth than other genres of written literature. As a result, the novel conveys political, social, and cultural themes to society through the stories and events presented in the specific novel. Mohamed Suleiman is one of the authors of Swahili novels who crafts various stories and events that present substantial themes for society. 4. The novel 'Kiu' is a Swahili novel that tells the story of Bahati, a young woman who was raised with care and is now encountering Idi, a deceitful man. Idi quickly entangles Bahati in the trap of false love. Lost in love and oblivious to herself, Bahati realizes that Idi does not truly love her, but rather loves himself, and that she, Bahati, is merely a tool for fulfilling his worldly desires. Like a bird caught in a trap, her efforts to find escape only bring her ruin. The novel 'Kiu' won first prize in the Kiswahili fiction writing competition, which was organized in 1970. 5. What is technique? Technique is the artistic craftsmanship employed by a writer when composing or narrating their literary work before the specific audience intended for that work. Technique encompasses elements such as use of language, structure, style, characters, and setting. Together, these elements enable the writer of a literary work to construct and convey their themes and ideas to the intended audience. The use of these technical elements varies, and may sometimes even be similar, from one writer to another. Mohamed Suleiman, in the novel 'Kiu', has employed various literary techniques to present the themes to the intended audience; however, in this work, we cannot address all of the techniques. Some of the artistic techniques we have examined in this work include the use of letters, suspense, proverbs, metaphors, and personification. 5.1.1 The Use of the Letter Technique  
A letter is an ancient means of communication between an individual and another individual, an individual and a group, an institution and an individual, or between institutions. Its aim is to convey information or a particular message that is important for the intended recipient to know.  
Idi received the letter with surprise because he was not expecting it. He turned the letter over and saw Bahati’s name written in hurried handwriting. He opened it and read:  
Idi,  
Don’t be surprised when I tell you that right now I am in bed with Mr. Mwinyi, and we are planning the day for our real wedding. It is not permitted to interfere with us because we have our own free will. I warn you for your own safety, that your plans should cease once you have received this letter. Send my regards to so-and-so … From the depths of my heart, Bahati. The letter ignited a fire in Idi’s heart and boiled him with anger. It struck him like a sudden, fierce storm. Suddenly his eyes changed color, his forehead became furrowed, and his jaw dropped, in a display of intense anguish. He read that letter again, and the more he read it, the angrier he became. 58-59). This letter was written by Bahati to Idi, her lover whom she loves very much, but here she is informing him that she is now in love with another person named Mwinyi. Mwinyi is Idi's boss, and Idi wanted Bahati to deceive Mwinyi by making him believe she loved him so that they could get money, while in reality, the one she truly loved was Idi. Now, it is truly shocking to see that the love between Mwinyi and Bahati has become genuine and not a joke as Idi had expected. Idi is now filled with great doubt about whether the wealth he hoped to gain from Mwinyi through Bahati will actually materialize, or if it has already been lost. The theme of love, as well as that of theft and smuggling, are greatly developed through the use of the letter mentioned above. Bahati is weighing whether Idi truly loves her, while Idi grows angry as his plan to gain Mwinyi's wealth through Bahati slips away. Also, through the above letter, the author develops the theme that not everything can turn out as one expects. Planning and implementation of something are two different things, although they are interdependent (Scott, 1995). Idi did not expect that telling Bahati to pretend to love Mwinyi so they could gain wealth would actually make Bahati truly fall in love with Mwinyi and leave him. Here, the theme of warnings is developed, emphasizing that love should not be experimented with, as at any moment it can change and become completely different from what was originally intended. Proverbs are expressions that are similar to and resemble sayings used by human beings as tools of communication (Msokile, 1992). However, proverbs often do not have two sides as is the case with sayings. A proverb, on its part, has two sides, where one side serves as a question and the other side provides the answer to the question posed (Wamitila, 2003). Proverbs are sayings that arise from expressions whose nature is that they emerge and disappear, and those that do not disappear but endure are what are called proverbs. Proverbs are a literary technique used by authors of literary works to underscore or emphasize a particular theme they want their audience to grasp. In his novel *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman has used proverbs in his work as follows: Things were not good for Idi, as his intention was not to truly love her but merely to toy with her. Most responsible parents know that when young people engage in romantic relationships before marriage, it often leads to them toying with each other and the issue of marriage gets lost. Therefore, as a parent, Cheusi wanted her daughter to end things with Idi immediately. The proverb used in the above passage has been employed to build and emphasize the theme of a mother's guidance to her child. Sociologists explain that habit is something that shapes character, and habits always persist (Ritzer, 2008). If in society girls and boys are left free to have relationships before marriage, they will consider it acceptable, and the issue of getting married will no longer hold any significance for them. Parents must fulfill their responsibilities properly so that members of society, especially the youth, see that having relationships before marriage is a bad thing that should never be encouraged. 5.1.3 The Use of Metaphor in Kiu

A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to compare two things with different characteristics without using any linking word of comparison, as is the case with simile (Kyando, 2013). The things being compared are considered to be entirely alike, without any differences. For example, one might say, “Mwajuma is a little rabbit hiding in a tree.” Here, Mwajuma is being compared to a rabbit as if they are two things that are exactly alike, without any difference at all. The main purpose of using metaphors in literary works is to emphasize the theme being presented to the reader. Mohamed Suleiman used a metaphor when he said:  
When people said that no one had ever outsmarted Mwinyi, their words were not exaggerated. Mwinyi had enough money to buy himself most of the things that a sixty-two-year-old man like him could desire, except for just one thing. That is what made him feel as though his entire life had been wasted, and that his wealth was like a rice cake that had been spoiled with sand (p.01). The words emphasized in ink in the phrase here express a saying that something good has now turned bad, something sweet has now become bitter, and something valuable has now lost its value. Mr. Mwinyi was a wealthy man who possessed all kinds of riches, but he longed to have a romantic relationship with a young woman named Bahati, whom he had come to love deeply. Every approach he tried failed to win Bahati over, leading him to complain that “his wealth was like a cake mixed with sand,” meaning his wealth did not help him at all and was of no benefit to him. Essentially, a rice cake that has sand mixed into it becomes inedible and loses all its flavor because the eater fears their teeth will bite into the sand. This saying has indeed been used to emphasize the theme of love—that if a person is wealthy in every material sense but lacks the love they long for, then their wealth becomes meaningless and causes them to live with more hardship and mental anguish than even a poor person. Sociologists acknowledge that there are certain things which are generally considered highly desirable to possess, such as wealth (Cross, 2011). However, there comes a time when a person lacks something they thought was minor, and their wealth does not help them obtain it, even though they believed their riches were the key to getting everything. This is akin to saying that the rice cake now has sand in it, for all of Mwinyi’s wealth could not enable him to win Bahati’s love. Another use of the saying appears when Cheusi, who is Bahati’s mother, was warning her daughter about her relationship with Idi. He says:
There was a brief but bitter silence. Then Cheusi continued to advise her: "That Idi of yours, let me tell you, he doesn't want you, he has nothing. Whoever truly desires a woman marries her. He just wants to toy with you and then discard you, moving on while laughing at you. I have already realized that just because you have studied your English you think I am ignorant, well then … One day you will cry like a dog, mouth raised, and I will be here (pp. 25–26).” In this passage the writer uses the saying, “you will cry like a dog, mouth raised,” to refer to the theme of guidance and warnings given by a mother to her child. Cheusi was warning her daughter Bahati about the relationship she had started with
At that moment, Iddi, her driver, entered without knocking. Mwinyi was startled and asked him, “Why are you late?” Iddi wiped his sweat to show the effort he had made, shook his head sadly, and said, “I found the door locked.” Those words broke Mwinyi’s heart. He slumped his shoulders and shrank into the chair, feeling that life was being unfair to him. Waiting without end—six months had passed, and relentless yearning weighed heavily upon him. He had already endured enough; yet he still did not know when the day of relief would come. But ah, her late mother’s words: “Whatever comes your way, accept it” (p. 02). The use of metaphor in the above phrase shows that words are compared to a knife or anything sharp that is capable of cutting something. “Those words struck Mwinyi to the core,” is a statement that shows Mwinyi’s hope of winning Bahati had vanished as soon as he received information from Idi that he could not find Bahati and that Bahati’s door was locked. Sociologists explain that a person may reach a point where they lose hope of obtaining something they have long desired but are unable to acquire (Webster, 2006). Losing hope in life is a bad thing because it can lead a person to do something harmful that may even endanger others. For example, Mwinyi's despair at not being able to have Bahati could drive him to make the decision to commit a crime such as rape. The act of rape is terrible for the victim but also for the perpetrator, as it can result in spending the rest of their life in prison. For a sixty-two-year-old man like Mwinyi to be imprisoned is a terrible thing that could cause him to die in prison. 5.1.4 The Use of Personification

However, it is said that the issue was actually a person’s temperament—and that person is arrogant and boastful. These descriptions show that the thing in question is not specified, which makes the keen reader want to find out what exactly it is that is troubling Mwinyi so much. The use of suspense will compel the reader to continue reading the novel 'Kiu' until they discover what it is that is bothering Mwinyi. As the reader continues, they come across the following words:  
Personification is a figure of speech used to give balance and the ability to act like humans to creatures or objects that do not possess such abilities (Mlacha, 1989). Things such as trees, words, insects, animals, and birds are depicted as performing human actions even though they do not have the ability to do so. For example, it is not unusual in literature to find birds courting, proposing marriage, and eventually getting married and living happily ever after (Senkoro, 2006). The use of personification in literary works is intended to build the theme in an imaginative way so that the reader reflects a little in order to grasp the intended theme of the author or narrator of the work before them. In the novel *Kiu*, there is the use of personification applied for this very purpose, as manifested in the following excerpt:
“People say that love never meets, but why have yours and Bahati’s?”
Bahati cried out with anguish and sorrow, until even sleep took pity on her, swiftly overtook her, and rested her on the bed. She was awakened by the clamoring of people going to the mosque, for dawn had already broken. Bahati’s sense of time was always guided by passersby. She had become accustomed to hearing the movements of people going to work, to school, to the mosque, passenger airplanes, and the calls to prayer (p.20). The words emphasized in the above passage are used as personification, because in real life only a human being is capable of showing compassion toward another person or creature. Sleep is a state in which a person loses consciousness, as expressed in the Swahili saying, "sleep is half of death." However, in the above passage, sleep appears to have been given the ability to feel compassion, as if it were human. 5.1.5 The Use of Suspense in Kiu

Suspense is a literary technique used by authors of literary works to craft their works in such a way that they effectively convey their intended themes to the target audience. This is a technique of delaying the reader from obtaining the solution or the truth of the matter, and making them continue reading until they encounter a solution or some explanation that will provide the answer they intended to find (Senkoro, 2006). The suspense technique is deliberately used by authors of literary works to give the reader or listener the desire to continue reading, especially when the work in question is lengthy enough to tire the reader. The length of the work will seem very short if there are suspenseful moments that captivate the reader. Suspense is an ancient literary technique that is widely used in oral literature and even in written literature. Mohamed Suleiman, in his novel *Kiu*, has employed this technique in the way he begins narrating his story. For example:

That evening, he was stretched out on a reclining chair, his eyes fixed on the ceiling, counting the minutes. His desire was not great, and the anxiety of failure had robbed him of joy. If only what he wanted was within his grasp, he would seize it and quench his thirst. If what he wanted could be bought with money, he would surely have scraped together every cent he had. But the thing itself depended on the will of another person, someone with taste and pride. So he had no choice but to ask and wait (pp. 01–02). This passage contains a sense of anxiety, as there is something that makes Mwinyi uncomfortable and torments him despite being wealthy. This is not stated explicitly, but it is merely mentioned that if obtaining that thing required money, Mwinyi would provide it.  
“Stop joking, Iddi,” Mwinyi scolded him. “Do you think a child like that could love an old man like me (p.05)?” In this passage, the tension built by the author on the first page of his novel begins to find answers on page five. This is where the issue that troubles Mwinyi is mentioned, to the extent that he lacks peace despite all his great wealth. That thing is none other than the love he had for a girl known by the name Bahati. Mwinyi was a man of sixty-two years, but he loved Bahati very much, even though she was a young girl who had not yet finished school. In this context, another tension arises: could Bahati agree to become the lover of an older man, just as Mwinyi did? This too creates suspense for the readers, who will be compelled to read further to find out what will happen regarding Mwinyi’s love for the young girl Bahati. The use of this technique of suspense has been employed with the aim of enhancing and developing the theme of love in the novel Kiu. This technique appears to be used repeatedly, as whenever the answer or solution to the initial suspense is found, another suspense is introduced (Mlacha, 1991). For example, in the excerpt above we find the solution that what had been troubling Mwinyi Raha and causing him sleepless nights was his love for Bahati's daughter. After realizing this, another anxiety has arisen as to whether such a young girl like Bahati could agree to be in a relationship with old Mwinyi, who could even be Bahati's father. Readers will continue reading until they find a solution, and after that, they will encounter another anxiety. Conclusion The specific objective of this work was to analyze and describe the stylistic techniques used to construct social themes in the novel "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman. Accordingly, the findings include the use of stylistic techniques such as letters, expressions, metaphors, personification, and anxiety. The research findings show that the novel 'Kiu' by Mohamed Suleiman is rich in stylistic techniques, but in this study we have focused only on the use of the letter-writing technique, sayings, metaphor, anxiety, and suspense. The main reason for selecting these five techniques is that they adequately meet the objectives of this research. The use of the letter-writing technique was employed with the aim of developing and advancing the theme of love, in which Bahati wanted to know if Iddi truly loved her. Bahati wrote a letter to inform Iddi that she was now genuinely in love with Mwinyi and asked Iddi not to bother her, as they were now planning their wedding. This letter tormented Iddi to the point where he did not know what to do, because he had already realized that all the plans he had made with Bahati were now ruined. However, the content of the letter was intended to test whether Iddi truly loved Bahati. Bahati knew that Iddi loved her because he became upset after reading the letter she had sent him. It turned out that Iddi was not upset because he really loved Bahati; rather, he saw clearly Some Stylistic Techniques in Swahili Novels: "The Novel Kiu by Mohamed Suleiman as an Example" Ali. Mwinyi’s plans to gain wealth through Bahati had become nothing more than an unattainable dream. Suspense is another artistic technique that has been used to highlight social themes in Mohamed Suleiman's novel Kiu. This technique has been employed in the arrangement of plots and events, where right from the beginning the novel starts with suspense. The situation of delaying the reader from finding the solution to what is being described in the novel creates in the reader a desire to read more, as they will want to continue reading in order to reach the conclusion of the event. For example, at the beginning of the novel, it is described that Mwinyi lives in hardship and lacks happiness despite being a wealthy person. The thing that is said to be depriving Mwinyi of happiness is his love for Bahati, something he believes cannot succeed because he is an old man and Bahati is a young woman. Other stylistic techniques used to develop social themes in the novel "Kiu" include proverbs, metaphors, and personification. M U H T A S A R I  
Kazi ya fasihi, ikiwa ni pamoja na riwaya, huundwa na mbinu pamoja na maudhui, mambo ambayo kwa pamoja ndiyo tunaita fasihi. Mbinu inaundwa na vipengele kama wahusika, mtindo, mazingira, muundo, na matumizi ya lugha. Vipengele hivi hutumiwa na waandishi kwa njia mbalimbali kulingana na ujuzi na uwezo wao. Kuhusiana na mbinu, inahusu mawazo makuu ya jumla yaliyoelezwa na mwandishi au msimulizi wa kazi ya fasihi na yaliyokusudiwa kupokelewa na hadhira. Kazi hii ililenga kuchunguza mada mbalimbali zilizowasilishwa na Mohamed Suleiman katika riwaya yake ya Kiswahili "Kiu." Kupitia riwaya hii, tumebaini na kujadili mbinu za kifasihi alizotumia mwandishi ili kuibua mada zilizomo ndani ya riwaya. 'Kiu' ni riwaya ya Kiswahili inayosimulia hadithi ya Bahati, msichana kijana aliyekuzwa kwa uangalifu na sasa anakutana na Idi, mwanamume mdanganyifu. Idi anamnasa Bahati haraka katika mtego wa mapenzi ya uongo. Wakati Bahati amezama sana katika mapenzi, bila kujitambua yeye mwenyewe wala mazingira yake, anagundua kwamba Idi hampendi kweli, bali anajipenda mwenyewe tu, na kwamba yeye, Bahati, ni chombo tu cha kutimiza matamanio yake ya kidunia. Aina ya riwaya hutumika kuelezea mambo kwa undani na upana zaidi kuliko aina nyingine za fasihi andishi. Hivyo basi, riwaya hubeba maudhui ya kisiasa, kijamii, na kitamaduni kwa jamii kupitia hadithi na matukio yanayowasilishwa katika riwaya husika. Mohamed Suleiman ni mmoja wa waandishi wa riwaya za Kiswahili ambaye huunda hadithi na matukio mbalimbali yanayowasilisha maudhui muhimu kwa jamii. Nne. Riwaya ya 'Kiu' ni riwaya ya Kiswahili inayosimulia kisa cha Bahati, msichana kijana aliyekuzwa kwa malezi bora na sasa anakutana na Idi, mwanaume mdanganyifu. Idi anamvuta Bahati haraka katika mtego wa mapenzi ya uongo. Akipotea katika mapenzi na kutomjua mwenyewe, Bahati anatambua kuwa Idi hampendi kwa kweli, bali anajipenda mwenyewe, na kwamba yeye, Bahati, ni chombo tu cha kutimiza matamanio yake ya kidunia. Kama ndege aliyenaswa kwenye mtego, jitihada zake za kutafuta njia ya kutoroka zinamletea maangamizi tu. Riwaya ya 'Kiu' ilishinda zawadi ya kwanza katika mashindano ya uandishi wa riwaya za Kiswahili, ambayo yaliandaliwa mwaka 1970. Tano. Tekni ni ustadi wa kisanii unaotumiwa na mwandishi anapoandika au kusimulia kazi yake ya fasihi mbele ya hadhira mahsusi iliyokusudiwa kwa kazi hiyo. Mbinu inajumuisha vipengele kama vile matumizi ya lugha, muundo, mtindo, wahusika, na mandhari. Pamoja, vipengele hivi humuwezesha mwandishi wa kazi ya fasihi kujenga na kuwasilisha mada na mawazo yao kwa hadhira lengwa. Matumizi ya vipengele hivi vya kiufundi hutofautiana, na wakati mwingine vinaweza kufanana, kutoka kwa mwandishi mmoja hadi mwingine. Mohamed Suleiman, katika riwaya ya 'Kiu', ametumia mbinu mbalimbali za kisanaa kuwasilisha mada kwa hadhira lengwa; hata hivyo, katika kazi hii, hatuwezi kujadili mbinu zote. Baadhi ya mbinu za kisanii tulizozichunguza katika kazi hii ni pamoja na matumizi ya barua, msisimko, methali, sitiari, na ufananisho. Mbinu inahusu ustadi wa kisanii unaotumiwa na mwandishi kuunda kazi yake ili wasomaji na wasikilizaji waifurahie (Njogu na Chimerah, 1999). Mbinu inaundwa na vipengele kama wahusika, mtindo, mazingira, muundo, na matumizi ya lugha. Vipengele hivi hutumiwa na waandishi kwa njia tofauti kulingana na ujuzi na utaalamu wao. (Simiyu, 2011). 5.1 Mbinu za Fasihi katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili  
5.1.1 Matumizi ya Mbinu ya Barua  
Barua ni njia ya zamani ya mawasiliano kati ya mtu mmoja na mwingine, mtu mmoja na kundi, taasisi na mtu mmoja, au kati ya taasisi. Lengo lake ni kuwasilisha taarifa au ujumbe maalumu ambao ni muhimu kwa mpokeaji aliyekusudiwa kuufahamu.  
Idi alipokea barua hiyo kwa mshangao kwa sababu hakuwa akiitarajia. Aligeuza barua na kuona jina la Bahati limeandikwa kwa mwandiko wa haraka. Akaifungua na kusoma:  
Idi,  
Usishangae nitakapokuambia kwamba sasa hivi nipo kitandani na Bwana Mwinyi, na tunapanga siku ya harusi yetu halisi. Hauruhusiwi kuingilia kati sisi kwa sababu tuna hiari yetu wenyewe. Ninakuonya kwa usalama wako mwenyewe, kwamba mipango yako inapaswa kusitishwa mara tu utakapopokea barua hii. Tafadhali fikisha salamu zangu kwa fulani... Kutoka katika kina cha moyo wangu, Bahati. Barua hiyo iliwasha moto moyoni mwa Idi na kumchemsha kwa hasira. Ilimpiga kama dhoruba kali ya ghafla. Ghafla macho yake yakabadilika rangi, paji lake la uso likakunja, na taya lake likashuka, akionyesha uchungu mkubwa. Alisoma barua hiyo tena, na kadri alivyokuwa akiisoma zaidi, ndivyo alivyokuwa akikasirika zaidi. 58-59). Barua hii iliandikwa na Bahati kwa Idi, mpenzi wake ambaye anampenda sana, lakini hapa anamjulisha kwamba sasa amependa mtu mwingine anayeitwa Mwinyi. Mwinyi ni bosi wa Idi, na Idi alitaka Bahati amdanganye Mwinyi kwa kumfanya aamini kwamba anampenda ili wapate pesa, ilhali kwa ukweli yule anayempenda kwa dhati ni Idi. Sasa, ni jambo la kushangaza sana kuona kwamba mapenzi kati ya Mwinyi na Bahati yamekuwa ya kweli na si mzaha kama Idi alivyotarajia. Idi sasa amejaa shaka kubwa kuhusu kama utajiri aliotarajia kupata kutoka kwa Mwinyi kupitia Bahati utatimia kweli, au tayari umepotea. Mada ya upendo, pamoja na ile ya wizi na magendo, zimeendelezwa sana kupitia matumizi ya barua iliyotajwa hapo juu. Bahati anatafakari kama Idi kweli anampenda, huku Idi akikasirika mpango wake wa kupata utajiri wa Mwinyi kupitia Bahati unavyokuwa ukitoweka. Pia, kupitia barua iliyo hapo juu, mwandishi anakuza dhamira kwamba si kila kitu kinaweza kutokea kama mtu anavyotarajia. Mipango na utekelezaji wa jambo fulani ni mambo mawili tofauti, ingawa yanategemeana (Scott, 1995). Idi hakutarajia kwamba kumuambia Bahati ajifanye kumpenda Mwinyi ili wapate utajiri kungepelekea Bahati kumpenda Mwinyi kweli na kumuacha yeye. Hapa, mada ya maonyo inaendelezwa, ikisisitiza kwamba mapenzi hayapaswi kujaribiwa, kwani wakati wowote yanaweza kubadilika na kuwa tofauti kabisa na vile ilivyokusudiwa awali. Baadhi ya Mbinu za Kisanii katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili: 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano — Ali. Methali ni misemo inayofanana na na kukaribia usemi unaotumiwa na binadamu kama nyenzo za mawasiliano (Msokile, 1992). Hata hivyo, methali mara nyingi hazina pande mbili kama ilivyo kwa misemo. Methali, kwa upande wake, ina pande mbili, ambapo upande mmoja unatumika kama swali na upande mwingine unatoa jibu kwa swali lililoulizwa (Wamitila, 2003). Methali ni misemo inayoibuka kutokana na maneno ambayo asili yake ni kwamba hujitokeza na kutoweka, na yale yasiyotoweka bali hudumu ndiyo yanayoitwa methali. Methali ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na waandishi wa kazi za fasihi ili kusisitiza au kuweka mkazo katika mada fulani wanayotaka hadhira yao ielewe. Katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman ametumia methali katika kazi yake kama ifuatavyo: Mambo hayakuwa mazuri kwa Idi, kwani nia yake haikuwa kumpenda kwa dhati bali tu kuchezea hisia zake. Wazazi wengi wenye kuwajibika wanajua kwamba vijana wanapojihusisha na uhusiano wa kimapenzi kabla ya ndoa, mara nyingi husababisha wao kuchezeana na suala la ndoa hupotea. Kwa hiyo, kama mzazi, Cheusi alitaka binti yake aweke kikomo mara moja kwa uhusiano na Idi. Methali iliyotumika katika kifungu hapo juu imetumika kujenga na kusisitiza mada ya mwongozo wa mama kwa mtoto wake. Wanajamii wanaeleza kwamba tabia ni kitu kinachoathiri tabia ya mtu, na tabia huendelea kuwepo daima (Ritzer, 2008). Ikiwa katika jamii wasichana na wavulana wataachwa huru kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa, wataona kuwa ni jambo linalokubalika, na suala la kuoa au kuolewa halitakuwa na maana yoyote kwao. Wazazi wanapaswa kutimiza majukumu yao ipasavyo ili wanajamii, hasa vijana, waone kwamba kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa ni jambo baya ambalo halipaswi kupewa moyo kamwe. 5.1.3 Matumizi ya Tafsida katika Kiu

Tafsida ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kulinganisha vitu viwili vyenye sifa tofauti bila kutumia neno lolote la kulinganisha, kama ilivyo kwa tashbihi (Kyando, 2013). Vitu vinavyolinganishwa huchukuliwa kuwa vinafanana kabisa, bila tofauti yoyote. Kwa mfano, mtu anaweza kusema, "Mwajuma ni sungura mdogo anayejificha kwenye mti." Hapa, Mwajuma analinganishwa na sungura kana kwamba wao ni vitu viwili ambavyo ni sawa kabisa, bila tofauti yoyote kabisa. Lengo kuu la kutumia tashbihi katika kazi za fasihi ni kusisitiza mada inayowasilishwa kwa msomaji. Mohamed Suleiman alitumia sitiari aliposema:  
Watu waliposema kwamba hakuna aliyewahi kumbwaga Mwinyi kwa ujanja, maneno yao hayakuwa ya kupindisha. Mwinyi alikuwa na pesa za kutosha kununua karibu kila kitu ambacho mwanaume wa miaka sitini na miwili kama yeye angeweza kutamani, isipokuwa kitu kimoja tu. Hicho ndicho kilichomfanya ajisikie kana kwamba maisha yake yote yamepotea bure, na kwamba utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki ya mchele iliyoharibiwa na mchanga (uk.01). Maneno yaliyosisitizwa kwa wino katika usemi hapa yanaonyesha methali kwamba jambo zuri sasa limekuwa baya, kitu kitamu sasa kimekuwa kichungu, na kitu cha thamani sasa kimepoteza thamani yake. Bwana Mwinyi alikuwa mtu tajiri aliyemiliki utajiri wa kila aina, lakini alitamani kuwa na uhusiano wa kimapenzi na msichana mchanga aitwaye Bahati, ambaye alimpenda sana. Kila jaribio alilofanya lilishindwa kumshawishi Bahati, jambo lililomfanya kulalamika kwamba “utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki iliyochanganywa na mchanga,” akimaanisha utajiri wake haukumsaidia kabisa na haukuwa na manufaa kwake. Kimsingi, keki ya mchele iliyochanganywa na mchanga inakuwa isiyoliwa na inapoteza ladha yake yote kwa sababu mla anahofu meno yake yatakutana na mchanga. Msemo huu kwa kweli umetumika kuangazia mada ya upendo—kwamba ikiwa mtu ana utajiri wa kila namna lakini anakosa upendo anaoutamani, basi utajiri wake unakuwa hauna maana na humfanya aishi kwa shida na mateso ya kiakili zaidi kuliko hata mtu maskini. Wanajamii wa sosholojia wanakubali kwamba kuna mambo fulani ambayo kwa ujumla yanachukuliwa kuwa yanatamanika sana kumiliki, kama vile utajiri (Cross, 2011). Hata hivyo, huwa inafika wakati ambapo mtu anakosa kitu alichodhani ni kidogo, na utajiri wake haumsaidii kukipata, ingawa aliamini utajiri wake ulikuwa ufunguo wa kupata kila kitu. Hii ni sawa na kusema kwamba keki ya mchele sasa ina mchanga ndani yake, kwani utajiri wote wa Mwinyi haukuweza kumwezesha kushinda mapenzi ya Bahati. Matumizi mengine ya msemo huo yanajitokeza wakati Cheusi, ambaye ni mama yake Bahati, alipokuwa akimwonya binti yake kuhusu uhusiano wake na Idi. Anasema:
Kulikuwa na kimya kifupi lakini chenye uchungu. Kisha Cheusi aliendelea kumpa ushauri: "Yule Idi wako, nikuambie, hakutaki, hana chochote. Yeyote anayemtamani mwanamke kwa dhati humuoa. Yeye anataka tu kukuchezea na kisha kukutupa, akiendelea mbele huku akikucheka. Nimegundua tayari kwamba kwa sababu tu umesoma Kiingereza chako unafikiri mimi ni mjinga, basi … Siku moja utalia kama mbwa, mdomo juu, na nitakuwa hapa (uk. 25–26)." Katika dondoo hili mwandishi anatumia msemo, "utalia kama mbwa, mdomo juu," kuonyesha dhamira ya maelekezo na onyo kutoka kwa mama kwa mtoto wake. Cheusi alikuwa akimwonya binti yake Bahati kuhusu uhusiano aliokuwa ameanzisha. Wakati huo huo, Iddi, dereva wake, aliingia bila kugonga. Mwinyi alishtuka na kumuuliza, "Kwa nini umechelewa?" Iddi alifuta jasho lake kuonyesha juhudi alizofanya, akatikisa kichwa kwa huzuni, na kusema, "Nilikuta mlango umefungwa." Maneno hayo yaliuumiza moyo wa Mwinyi. Aliinamisha mabega yake na kujikunyata kwenye kiti, akihisi kwamba maisha yalikuwa hayamtendei haki. Kusubiri bila mwisho—miezi sita ilikuwa imepita, na shauku isiyokoma ilimlemea sana. Alikuwa tayari amevumilia vya kutosha; lakini bado hakujua ni lini siku ya faraja ingefika. Lakini ah, maneno ya marehemu mama yake: “Chochote kitakachokuja, kikubali” (uk. 02). Matumizi ya sitiari katika kifungu hapo juu yanaonyesha kwamba maneno yamefananishwa na kisu au kitu chochote chenye makali kinachoweza kukata kitu. "Maneno hayo yalimgonga Mwinyi hadi kwenye moyo wake," ni tamko linaloonyesha kuwa matumaini ya Mwinyi ya kumshinda Bahati yalitoweka mara tu alipoupata ujumbe kutoka kwa Idi kwamba hakuweza kumpata Bahati na kwamba mlango wa Bahati ulikuwa umefungwa. Wanajamii wanaeleza kwamba mtu anaweza kufikia hatua ambapo anakata tamaa ya kupata kitu ambacho amekuwa akikitamani kwa muda mrefu lakini hawezi kukipata (Webster, 2006). Kupoteza matumaini katika maisha ni jambo baya kwa sababu linaweza kumfanya mtu afanye kitu hatari ambacho kinaweza hata kuhatarisha wengine. Kwa mfano, kukata tamaa kwa Mwinyi kwa kushindwa kumpata Bahati kunaweza kumpelekea kufanya uamuzi wa kutenda kosa kama ubakaji. Kitendo cha ubakaji ni kibaya sana kwa mwathirika lakini pia kwa mtendaji, kwani kinaweza kusababisha kutumia maisha yake yote gerezani. Kwa mwanaume mwenye umri wa miaka sitini na miwili kama Mwinyi kufungwa gerezani ni jambo baya sana linaloweza kusababisha afe gerezani. 5.1.4 Matumizi ya Uhusishaji wa Mambo kwa Sifa za Kibinadamu  
JOHS Juzuu ya 22 Na. Baadhi ya Mbinu za Kisanaa katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili: "Riwaya ya Kiswahili 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano" Ali. pesa zote kutoka kwa utajiri wake. Hata hivyo, inasemekana kwamba tatizo halisi lilikuwa tabia ya mtu—na mtu huyo ni mwenye kiburi na anayejisifu. Maelezo haya yanaonyesha kwamba kitu kinachozungumziwa hakijabainishwa, jambo ambalo humfanya msomaji makini kutaka kujua hasa nini kinachomsumbua Mwinyi sana. Matumizi ya mbinu ya msisimko yatawalazimisha wasomaji kuendelea kusoma riwaya ya 'Kiu' hadi watakapogundua nini hasa kinachomsumbua Mwinyi. Mtu anapoendelea kusoma, anakutana na maneno yafuatayo:  
Uhakiki ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kutoa uwiano na uwezo wa kutenda kama binadamu kwa viumbe au vitu visivyo na uwezo huo (Mlacha, 1989). Mambo kama vile miti, maneno, wadudu, wanyama, na ndege yanaonyeshwa yakifanya matendo ya kibinadamu ingawa hayana uwezo wa kufanya hivyo. Kwa mfano, si jambo la ajabu katika fasihi kukuta ndege wakichumbiana, wakiposa, na hatimaye wakioana na kuishi kwa furaha milele (Senkoro, 2006). Matumizi ya ufananisho katika kazi za fasihi yanalenga kujenga mada kwa njia ya kubuni ili msomaji atafakari kidogo ili kuelewa mada iliyokusudiwa na mwandishi au msimulizi wa kazi hiyo iliyo mbele yao. Katika riwaya *Kiu*, matumizi ya uhawilishaji yamechukuliwa kwa lengo hili, kama inavyoonekana katika dondoo lifuatalo:  
"Watu husema kwamba mapenzi hayatani, lakini kwa nini yako na ya Bahati yakakutana?"  
Bahati alipiga yowe kwa maumivu na huzuni, hadi hata usingizi ulimhurumia, ukamshika haraka, ukamlaza kitandani. Alikuwa ameamusha na makelele ya watu wanaokwenda msikitini, kwa maana alfajiri ilikuwa imeshapambazuka. Hisia ya muda ya Bahati ilikuwa ikiendeshwa kila wakati na wapita njia. Alikuwa amezoea kusikia harakati za watu waendao kazini, shuleni, msikitini, ndege za abiria, na mwito wa sala (uk.20). Maneno yaliyosisitizwa katika kifungu hapo juu yanatumika kama ufananisho wa kutoa uhai kwa kitu kisicho na uhai, kwa sababu katika maisha halisi ni binadamu pekee anayeweza kuonyesha huruma kwa mtu mwingine au kiumbe. Usingizi ni hali ambayo mtu hupoteza fahamu, kama inavyoelezwa katika msemo wa Kiswahili, "usingizi ni nusu ya kifo." Hata hivyo, katika kifungu hicho hapo juu, usingizi unaonekana kupewa uwezo wa kuhisi huruma, kana kwamba ni binadamu. Suto ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na waandishi wa kazi za fasihi kutunga kazi zao kwa namna ambayo zinawasilisha kwa ufanisi dhamira walizokusudia kwa hadhira lengwa. Hii ni mbinu ya kuchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhisho au ukweli wa jambo fulani, na kumfanya aendelee kusoma hadi akumbane na suluhisho au maelezo fulani yatakayotoa jibu alilokusudia kulipata (Senkoro, 2006). Mbinu ya kusisimua hutumiwa makusudi na waandishi wa kazi za fasihi ili kumpa msomaji au msikilizaji hamu ya kuendelea kusoma, hasa pale kazi husika inapokuwa ndefu kiasi cha kumchosha msomaji. Urefu wa kazi utaonekana kuwa mfupi sana ikiwa kuna nyakati za kusisimua zinazomvutia msomaji. Msisimko ni mbinu ya zamani ya fasihi ambayo inatumika sana katika fasihi simulizi na hata katika fasihi andishi. Mohamed Suleiman, katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, ametumia mbinu hii katika namna anavyoanza kusimulia hadithi yake. Kwa mfano:

Jioni hiyo, alikuwa amelala kwenye kiti cha ku reclining, macho yake yamekazia kwenye dari, akihesabu dakika. Tamaa yake haikuwa kubwa, na wasiwasi wa kushindwa ulikuwa umeondoa furaha yake. Laiti kile alichotaka kingekuwa mikononi mwake, angekikamata na kutuliza kiu yake. Kama kile alichokitaka kingeweza kununuliwa kwa pesa, angekuwa amekusanya kila senti aliyokuwa nayo. Lakini kitu chenyewe kilitegemea mapenzi ya mtu mwingine, mtu mwenye ladha na fahari. Kwa hiyo hakuwa na chaguo ila kuuliza na kusubiri (uk. 01–02). Dondoo hii ina hisia ya wasiwasi, kwani kuna kitu kinachomfanya Mwinyi ajisikie vibaya na kumtesa licha ya kuwa na utajiri. Hili halijasemwa waziwazi, bali imetajwa tu kwamba kama kupata kitu hicho kungehitaji pesa, Mwinyi angekitoa.  
"Acha utani, Iddi," Mwinyi alimkemea. "Je, unafikiri mtoto kama huyo anaweza kumpenda mzee kama mimi (uk.05)?" Katika kifungu hiki, mvutano ulioumbwa na mwandishi kwenye ukurasa wa kwanza wa riwaya yake unaanza kupata majibu ukurasa wa tano. Hapa ndipo tatizo linalomsumbua Mwinyi linapotajwa, kiasi kwamba hana amani licha ya utajiri wake mkubwa. Kitu hicho si kingine bali ni upendo aliokuwa nao kwa msichana anayeitwa Bahati. Mwinyi alikuwa mwanaume wa miaka sitini na miwili, lakini alipenda sana Bahati, ingawa alikuwa msichana mdogo ambaye bado hakuwa amemaliza shule. Katika muktadha huu, mvutano mwingine unatokea: je, Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa mpenzi wa mwanaume mzee, kama vile Mwinyi alivyofanya? Hili pia linazua msisimko kwa wasomaji, ambao watalazimika kuendelea kusoma ili kujua nini kitatokea kuhusu mapenzi ya Mwinyi kwa msichana mdogo Bahati. Matumizi ya mbinu hii ya wasiwasi yametumika kwa lengo la kuimarisha na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi katika riwaya ya Kiu. Mbinu hii inaonekana kutumiwa mara kwa mara, kwani kila mara jibu au suluhisho la msisimko wa awali linapopatikana, msisimko mwingine unaanzishwa (Mlacha, 1991). Kwa mfano, katika dondoo hapo juu tunapata suluhisho kwamba kilichokuwa kinamsumbua Mwinyi Raha na kumsababishia kukosa usingizi usiku ilikuwa ni mapenzi yake kwa binti wa Bahati. Baada ya kutambua hili, hofu nyingine imezuka kuhusu kama msichana mchanga kama Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa kwenye uhusiano na Mwinyi mzee, ambaye hata angeweza kuwa baba yake Bahati. Wasomaji wataendelea kusoma hadi watakapopata suluhisho, na baada ya hapo, watakutana na wasiwasi mwingine. Hitimisho Lengo mahususi la kazi hii lilikuwa kuchambua na kuelezea mbinu za kisanaa zilizotumiwa kujenga dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya "Kiu" ya Mohamed Suleiman. Hivyo basi, matokeo yanajumuisha matumizi ya mbinu za kisanaa kama barua, misemo, tashihisi, ufananisho, na wasiwasi. Matokeo ya utafiti yanaonyesha kuwa riwaya ya 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman imejaa mbinu za kisanaa, lakini katika utafiti huu tumejikita tu kwenye matumizi ya mbinu ya uandishi wa barua, methali, sitiari, wasiwasi, na msisimko. Sababu kuu ya kuchagua mbinu hizi tano ni kwamba zinakidhi ipasavyo malengo ya utafiti huu. Matumizi ya mbinu ya kuandika barua yalitumiwa kwa lengo la kuendeleza na kukuza dhamira ya mapenzi, ambapo Bahati alitaka kujua kama Iddi kweli anampenda. Bahati aliandika barua kumjulisha Iddi kwamba sasa anampenda Mwinyi kwa dhati na akamwomba Iddi amwache, kwani sasa walikuwa wanapanga harusi yao. Barua hii ilimsumbua Iddi hadi akashindwa kujua la kufanya, kwa sababu tayari aligundua kwamba mipango yote aliyokuwa amefanya na Bahati sasa imeharibika. Hata hivyo, yaliyomo kwenye barua hiyo yalilenga kujaribu kama Iddi kweli anampenda Bahati. Bahati alijua kwamba Iddi alimpenda kwa sababu alikasirika baada ya kusoma barua aliyomtumia. Ilibainika kuwa Iddi hakuwa amekasirika kwa sababu alimpenda sana Bahati; bali, aliona wazi kabisa Baadhi ya mbinu za kisanii katika riwaya za Kiswahili: "Riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano" na Ali. Mipango ya Mwinyi ya kupata utajiri kupitia Bahati ilikuwa imebaki kuwa ndoto isiyoweza kufikiwa. Msisimko ni mbinu nyingine ya kisanii iliyotumika kuangazia mada za kijamii katika riwaya ya Mohamed Suleiman, Kiu. Mbinu hii imetumika katika upangaji wa njama na matukio, ambapo tangu mwanzo riwaya inaanza kwa msisimko. Hali ya kumchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhisho la kile kinachoelezewa katika riwaya humfanya msomaji atamani kusoma zaidi, kwani atataka kuendelea kusoma ili afikie hitimisho la tukio. Kwa mfano, mwanzoni mwa riwaya, inaelezwa kuwa Mwinyi anaishi kwenye matatizo na anakosa furaha licha ya kuwa mtu tajiri. Kitu kinachosemekana kinamnyima Mwinyi furaha ni upendo wake kwa Bahati, jambo ambalo anaamini haliwezi kufanikiwa kwa sababu yeye ni mzee na Bahati ni mwanamke mchanga. Mbinu nyingine za kisanii zilizotumika kuendeleza dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya "Kiu" ni pamoja na nahau, methali, na uchanganuzi wa mtu. Keywords: Novel, Written Literature, Technical Techniques, Style, Literature

A B S T R A C T
A work of literature, including a novel, is formed by technique and content, which together constitute what we refer to as literature. Technique is composed of elements such as characters, style, setting, structure, and the use of language. These elements are utilized by writers in various ways depending on their skills and abilities.

5.1 Literary Techniques in the Swahili Novel  
5.1.1 The Use of the Letter Technique  
A letter is an ancient means of communication between an individual and another individual, an individual and a group, an institution and an individual, or between institutions. Its aim is to convey information or a particular message that is important for the intended recipient to know.  
Idi received the letter with surprise because he was not expecting it.
discourses.translated_txt:
5.1 Mbinu za Fasihi katika Riwaya ya Kiswahili  
5.1.1 Matumizi ya Mbinu ya Barua  
Barua ni njia ya zamani ya mawasiliano kati ya mtu mmoja na mwingine, mtu mmoja na kundi, taasisi na mtu mmoja, au kati ya taasisi. Lengo lake ni kuwasilisha taarifa au ujumbe maalumu ambao ni muhimu kwa mpokeaji aliyekusudiwa kuufahamu.  
Idi alipokea barua hiyo kwa mshangao kwa sababu hakuwa akiitarajia.

He turned the letter over and saw Bahati’s name written in hurried handwriting. He opened it and read:

Don’t be surprised when I tell you that right now I am in bed with Mr. Mwinyi, and we are planning the day for our real wedding.

5.1.2 The Use of Proverbs in Kiu

Proverbs are expressions that are similar to and resemble sayings used by human beings as tools of communication (Msokile, 1992).
discourses.translated_txt: Methali ni misemo inayofanana na na kukaribia usemi unaotumiwa na binadamu kama nyenzo za mawasiliano (Msokile, 1992).

discourses.source_txt: However, proverbs often do not have two sides as is the case with sayings.
discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, methali mara nyingi hazina pande mbili kama ilivyo kwa misemo.

discourses.source_txt: A proverb, on its part, has two sides, where one side serves as a question and the other side provides the answer to the question posed (Wamitila, 2003).
discourses.translated_txt: Methali, kwa upande wake, ina pande mbili, ambapo upande mmoja unatumika kama swali na upande mwingine unatoa jibu kwa swali lililoulizwa (Wamitila, 2003).

discourses.source_txt: Proverbs are sayings that arise from expressions whose nature is that they emerge and disappear, and those that do not disappear but endure are what are called proverbs.
discourses.translated_txt: Methali ni misemo inayoibuka kutokana na maneno ambayo asili yake ni kwamba hujitokeza na kutoweka, na yale yasiyotoweka bali hudumu ndiyo yanayoitwa methali.

discourses.source_txt: Proverbs are a literary technique used by authors of literary works to underscore or emphasize a particular theme they want their audience to grasp.
discourses.translated_txt: Methali ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na waandishi wa kazi za fasihi ili kusisitiza au kuweka mkazo katika mada fulani wanayotaka hadhira yao ielewe.

discourses.source_txt: In his novel *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman has used proverbs in his work as follows: Things were not good for Idi, as his intention was not to truly love her but merely to toy with her.
discourses.translated_txt: Katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, Mohamed Suleiman ametumia methali katika kazi yake kama ifuatavyo: Mambo hayakuwa mazuri kwa Idi, kwani nia yake haikuwa kumpenda kwa dhati bali tu kuchezea hisia zake.

discourses.source_txt: Most responsible parents know that when young people engage in romantic relationships before marriage, it often leads to them toying with each other and the issue of marriage gets lost. Therefore, as a parent, Cheusi wanted her daughter to end things with Idi immediately.
discourses.translated_txt: Wazazi wengi wenye kuwajibika wanajua kwamba vijana wanapojihusisha na uhusiano wa kimapenzi kabla ya ndoa, mara nyingi husababisha wao kuchezeana na suala la ndoa hupotea. Kwa hiyo, kama mzazi, Cheusi alitaka binti yake aweke kikomo mara moja kwa uhusiano na Idi.

discourses.source_txt: The proverb used in the above passage has been employed to build and emphasize the theme of a mother's guidance to her child.
discourses.translated_txt: Methali iliyotumika katika kifungu hapo juu imetumika kujenga na kusisitiza mada ya mwongozo wa mama kwa mtoto wake.

discourses.source_txt: Sociologists explain that habit is something that shapes character, and habits always persist (Ritzer, 2008).
discourses.translated_txt: Wanajamii wanaeleza kwamba tabia ni kitu kinachoathiri tabia ya mtu, na tabia huendelea kuwepo daima (Ritzer, 2008).

discourses.source_txt: If in society girls and boys are left free to have relationships before marriage, they will consider it acceptable, and the issue of getting married will no longer hold any significance for them. Parents must fulfill their responsibilities properly so that members of society, especially the youth, see that having relationships before marriage is a bad thing that should never be encouraged.
discourses.translated_txt: Ikiwa katika jamii wasichana na wavulana wataachwa huru kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa, wataona kuwa ni jambo linalokubalika, na suala la kuoa au kuolewa halitakuwa na maana yoyote kwao. Wazazi wanapaswa kutimiza majukumu yao ipasavyo ili wanajamii, hasa vijana, waone kwamba kuwa na mahusiano kabla ya ndoa ni jambo baya ambalo halipaswi kupewa moyo kamwe.

discourses.source_txt:
5.1.3 The Use of Metaphor in Kiu

A metaphor is a figure of speech that is used to compare two things with different characteristics without using any linking word of comparison, as is the case with simile (Kyando, 2013). The things being compared are considered to be entirely alike, without any differences.
discourses.translated_txt:
5.1.3 Matumizi ya Tafsida katika Kiu

Tafsida ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kulinganisha vitu viwili vyenye sifa tofauti bila kutumia neno lolote la kulinganisha, kama ilivyo kwa tashbihi (Kyando, 2013). Vitu vinavyolinganishwa huchukuliwa kuwa vinafanana kabisa, bila tofauti yoyote.

discourses.source_txt: For example, one might say, “Mwajuma is a little rabbit hiding in a tree.” Here, Mwajuma is being compared to a rabbit as if they are two things that are exactly alike, without any difference at all.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mfano, mtu anaweza kusema, "Mwajuma ni sungura mdogo anayejificha kwenye mti." Hapa, Mwajuma analinganishwa na sungura kana kwamba wao ni vitu viwili ambavyo ni sawa kabisa, bila tofauti yoyote kabisa.

discourses.source_txt: The main purpose of using metaphors in literary works is to emphasize the theme being presented to the reader.
discourses.translated_txt: Lengo kuu la kutumia tashbihi katika kazi za fasihi ni kusisitiza mada inayowasilishwa kwa msomaji.

discourses.source_txt:
Mohamed Suleiman used a metaphor when he said:  
When people said that no one had ever outsmarted Mwinyi, their words were not exaggerated. Mwinyi had enough money to buy himself most of the things that a sixty-two-year-old man like him could desire, except for just one thing.
discourses.translated_txt:
Mohamed Suleiman alitumia sitiari aliposema:  
Watu waliposema kwamba hakuna aliyewahi kumbwaga Mwinyi kwa ujanja, maneno yao hayakuwa ya kupindisha. Mwinyi alikuwa na pesa za kutosha kununua karibu kila kitu ambacho mwanaume wa miaka sitini na miwili kama yeye angeweza kutamani, isipokuwa kitu kimoja tu.

discourses.source_txt: That is what made him feel as though his entire life had been wasted, and that his wealth was like a rice cake that had been spoiled with sand (p.01).
discourses.translated_txt: Hicho ndicho kilichomfanya ajisikie kana kwamba maisha yake yote yamepotea bure, na kwamba utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki ya mchele iliyoharibiwa na mchanga (uk.01).

discourses.source_txt: The words emphasized in ink in the phrase here express a saying that something good has now turned bad, something sweet has now become bitter, and something valuable has now lost its value.
discourses.translated_txt: Maneno yaliyosisitizwa kwa wino katika usemi hapa yanaonyesha methali kwamba jambo zuri sasa limekuwa baya, kitu kitamu sasa kimekuwa kichungu, na kitu cha thamani sasa kimepoteza thamani yake.

discourses.source_txt: Mr. Mwinyi was a wealthy man who possessed all kinds of riches, but he longed to have a romantic relationship with a young woman named Bahati, whom he had come to love deeply. Every approach he tried failed to win Bahati over, leading him to complain that “his wealth was like a cake mixed with sand,” meaning his wealth did not help him at all and was of no benefit to him.
discourses.translated_txt: Bwana Mwinyi alikuwa mtu tajiri aliyemiliki utajiri wa kila aina, lakini alitamani kuwa na uhusiano wa kimapenzi na msichana mchanga aitwaye Bahati, ambaye alimpenda sana. Kila jaribio alilofanya lilishindwa kumshawishi Bahati, jambo lililomfanya kulalamika kwamba “utajiri wake ulikuwa kama keki iliyochanganywa na mchanga,” akimaanisha utajiri wake haukumsaidia kabisa na haukuwa na manufaa kwake.

discourses.source_txt: Essentially, a rice cake that has sand mixed into it becomes inedible and loses all its flavor because the eater fears their teeth will bite into the sand.
discourses.translated_txt: Kimsingi, keki ya mchele iliyochanganywa na mchanga inakuwa isiyoliwa na inapoteza ladha yake yote kwa sababu mla anahofu meno yake yatakutana na mchanga.

discourses.source_txt: This saying has indeed been used to emphasize the theme of love—that if a person is wealthy in every material sense but lacks the love they long for, then their wealth becomes meaningless and causes them to live with more hardship and mental anguish than even a poor person.
discourses.translated_txt: Msemo huu kwa kweli umetumika kuangazia mada ya upendo—kwamba ikiwa mtu ana utajiri wa kila namna lakini anakosa upendo anaoutamani, basi utajiri wake unakuwa hauna maana na humfanya aishi kwa shida na mateso ya kiakili zaidi kuliko hata mtu maskini.

discourses.source_txt: Sociologists acknowledge that there are certain things which are generally considered highly desirable to possess, such as wealth (Cross, 2011).
discourses.translated_txt: Wanajamii wa sosholojia wanakubali kwamba kuna mambo fulani ambayo kwa ujumla yanachukuliwa kuwa yanatamanika sana kumiliki, kama vile utajiri (Cross, 2011).

discourses.source_txt: However, there comes a time when a person lacks something they thought was minor, and their wealth does not help them obtain it, even though they believed their riches were the key to getting everything.
discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, huwa inafika wakati ambapo mtu anakosa kitu alichodhani ni kidogo, na utajiri wake haumsaidii kukipata, ingawa aliamini utajiri wake ulikuwa ufunguo wa kupata kila kitu.

discourses.source_txt: This is akin to saying that the rice cake now has sand in it, for all of Mwinyi’s wealth could not enable him to win Bahati’s love.
discourses.translated_txt: Hii ni sawa na kusema kwamba keki ya mchele sasa ina mchanga ndani yake, kwani utajiri wote wa Mwinyi haukuweza kumwezesha kushinda mapenzi ya Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Another use of the saying appears when Cheusi, who is Bahati’s mother, was warning her daughter about her relationship with Idi.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi mengine ya msemo huo yanajitokeza wakati Cheusi, ambaye ni mama yake Bahati, alipokuwa akimwonya binti yake kuhusu uhusiano wake na Idi.

discourses.source_txt:
He says:
There was a brief but bitter silence.
discourses.translated_txt:
Anasema:
Kulikuwa na kimya kifupi lakini chenye uchungu.

discourses.source_txt: Then Cheusi continued to advise her: "That Idi of yours, let me tell you, he doesn't want you, he has nothing.
discourses.translated_txt: Kisha Cheusi aliendelea kumpa ushauri: "Yule Idi wako, nikuambie, hakutaki, hana chochote.

discourses.source_txt: Whoever truly desires a woman marries her. He just wants to toy with you and then discard you, moving on while laughing at you.
discourses.translated_txt: Yeyote anayemtamani mwanamke kwa dhati humuoa. Yeye anataka tu kukuchezea na kisha kukutupa, akiendelea mbele huku akikucheka.

discourses.source_txt:
I have already realized that just because you have studied your English you think I am ignorant, well then … One day you will cry like a dog, mouth raised, and I will be here (pp. 25–26).” In this passage the writer uses the saying, “you will cry like a dog, mouth raised,” to refer to the theme of guidance and warnings given by a mother to her child. Cheusi was warning her daughter Bahati about the relationship she had started with
At that moment, Iddi, her driver, entered without knocking. Mwinyi was startled and asked him, “Why are you late?” Iddi wiped his sweat to show the effort he had made, shook his head sadly, and said, “I found the door locked.” Those words broke Mwinyi’s heart.
discourses.translated_txt: Nimegundua tayari kwamba kwa sababu tu umesoma Kiingereza chako unafikiri mimi ni mjinga, basi … Siku moja utalia kama mbwa, mdomo juu, na nitakuwa hapa (uk. 25–26)." Katika dondoo hili mwandishi anatumia msemo, "utalia kama mbwa, mdomo juu," kuonyesha dhamira ya maelekezo na onyo kutoka kwa mama kwa mtoto wake. Cheusi alikuwa akimwonya binti yake Bahati kuhusu uhusiano aliokuwa ameanzisha. Wakati huo huo, Iddi, dereva wake, aliingia bila kugonga. Mwinyi alishtuka na kumuuliza, "Kwa nini umechelewa?" Iddi alifuta jasho lake kuonyesha juhudi alizofanya, akatikisa kichwa kwa huzuni, na kusema, "Nilikuta mlango umefungwa." Maneno hayo yaliuumiza moyo wa Mwinyi.

discourses.source_txt: He slumped his shoulders and shrank into the chair, feeling that life was being unfair to him.
discourses.translated_txt: Aliinamisha mabega yake na kujikunyata kwenye kiti, akihisi kwamba maisha yalikuwa hayamtendei haki.

discourses.source_txt: Waiting without end—six months had passed, and relentless yearning weighed heavily upon him. He had already endured enough; yet he still did not know when the day of relief would come.
discourses.translated_txt: Kusubiri bila mwisho—miezi sita ilikuwa imepita, na shauku isiyokoma ilimlemea sana. Alikuwa tayari amevumilia vya kutosha; lakini bado hakujua ni lini siku ya faraja ingefika.

discourses.source_txt: But ah, her late mother’s words: “Whatever comes your way, accept it” (p. 02).
discourses.translated_txt: Lakini ah, maneno ya marehemu mama yake: “Chochote kitakachokuja, kikubali” (uk. 02).

discourses.source_txt: The use of metaphor in the above phrase shows that words are compared to a knife or anything sharp that is capable of cutting something.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi ya sitiari katika kifungu hapo juu yanaonyesha kwamba maneno yamefananishwa na kisu au kitu chochote chenye makali kinachoweza kukata kitu.

discourses.source_txt: “Those words struck Mwinyi to the core,” is a statement that shows Mwinyi’s hope of winning Bahati had vanished as soon as he received information from Idi that he could not find Bahati and that Bahati’s door was locked.
discourses.translated_txt: "Maneno hayo yalimgonga Mwinyi hadi kwenye moyo wake," ni tamko linaloonyesha kuwa matumaini ya Mwinyi ya kumshinda Bahati yalitoweka mara tu alipoupata ujumbe kutoka kwa Idi kwamba hakuweza kumpata Bahati na kwamba mlango wa Bahati ulikuwa umefungwa.

discourses.source_txt: Sociologists explain that a person may reach a point where they lose hope of obtaining something they have long desired but are unable to acquire (Webster, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Wanajamii wanaeleza kwamba mtu anaweza kufikia hatua ambapo anakata tamaa ya kupata kitu ambacho amekuwa akikitamani kwa muda mrefu lakini hawezi kukipata (Webster, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: Losing hope in life is a bad thing because it can lead a person to do something harmful that may even endanger others. For example, Mwinyi's despair at not being able to have Bahati could drive him to make the decision to commit a crime such as rape.
discourses.translated_txt: Kupoteza matumaini katika maisha ni jambo baya kwa sababu linaweza kumfanya mtu afanye kitu hatari ambacho kinaweza hata kuhatarisha wengine. Kwa mfano, kukata tamaa kwa Mwinyi kwa kushindwa kumpata Bahati kunaweza kumpelekea kufanya uamuzi wa kutenda kosa kama ubakaji.

discourses.source_txt: The act of rape is terrible for the victim but also for the perpetrator, as it can result in spending the rest of their life in prison.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitendo cha ubakaji ni kibaya sana kwa mwathirika lakini pia kwa mtendaji, kwani kinaweza kusababisha kutumia maisha yake yote gerezani.

discourses.source_txt: For a sixty-two-year-old man like Mwinyi to be imprisoned is a terrible thing that could cause him to die in prison.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mwanaume mwenye umri wa miaka sitini na miwili kama Mwinyi kufungwa gerezani ni jambo baya sana linaloweza kusababisha afe gerezani.

discourses.translated_txt: Hata hivyo, inasemekana kwamba tatizo halisi lilikuwa tabia ya mtu—na mtu huyo ni mwenye kiburi na anayejisifu.

discourses.source_txt: These descriptions show that the thing in question is not specified, which makes the keen reader want to find out what exactly it is that is troubling Mwinyi so much. The use of suspense will compel the reader to continue reading the novel 'Kiu' until they discover what it is that is bothering Mwinyi.
discourses.translated_txt: Maelezo haya yanaonyesha kwamba kitu kinachozungumziwa hakijabainishwa, jambo ambalo humfanya msomaji makini kutaka kujua hasa nini kinachomsumbua Mwinyi sana. Matumizi ya mbinu ya msisimko yatawalazimisha wasomaji kuendelea kusoma riwaya ya 'Kiu' hadi watakapogundua nini hasa kinachomsumbua Mwinyi.

discourses.source_txt:
As the reader continues, they come across the following words:  
Personification is a figure of speech used to give balance and the ability to act like humans to creatures or objects that do not possess such abilities (Mlacha, 1989).
discourses.translated_txt:
Mtu anapoendelea kusoma, anakutana na maneno yafuatayo:  
Uhakiki ni tamathali ya usemi inayotumika kutoa uwiano na uwezo wa kutenda kama binadamu kwa viumbe au vitu visivyo na uwezo huo (Mlacha, 1989).

discourses.source_txt: Things such as trees, words, insects, animals, and birds are depicted as performing human actions even though they do not have the ability to do so. For example, it is not unusual in literature to find birds courting, proposing marriage, and eventually getting married and living happily ever after (Senkoro, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Mambo kama vile miti, maneno, wadudu, wanyama, na ndege yanaonyeshwa yakifanya matendo ya kibinadamu ingawa hayana uwezo wa kufanya hivyo. Kwa mfano, si jambo la ajabu katika fasihi kukuta ndege wakichumbiana, wakiposa, na hatimaye wakioana na kuishi kwa furaha milele (Senkoro, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: The use of personification in literary works is intended to build the theme in an imaginative way so that the reader reflects a little in order to grasp the intended theme of the author or narrator of the work before them.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi ya ufananisho katika kazi za fasihi yanalenga kujenga mada kwa njia ya kubuni ili msomaji atafakari kidogo ili kuelewa mada iliyokusudiwa na mwandishi au msimulizi wa kazi hiyo iliyo mbele yao.

discourses.source_txt:
In the novel *Kiu*, there is the use of personification applied for this very purpose, as manifested in the following excerpt:
“People say that love never meets, but why have yours and Bahati’s?”
Bahati cried out with anguish and sorrow, until even sleep took pity on her, swiftly overtook her, and rested her on the bed.
discourses.translated_txt:
Katika riwaya *Kiu*, matumizi ya uhawilishaji yamechukuliwa kwa lengo hili, kama inavyoonekana katika dondoo lifuatalo:  
"Watu husema kwamba mapenzi hayatani, lakini kwa nini yako na ya Bahati yakakutana?"  
Bahati alipiga yowe kwa maumivu na huzuni, hadi hata usingizi ulimhurumia, ukamshika haraka, ukamlaza kitandani.

discourses.source_txt: She was awakened by the clamoring of people going to the mosque, for dawn had already broken.
discourses.translated_txt: Alikuwa ameamusha na makelele ya watu wanaokwenda msikitini, kwa maana alfajiri ilikuwa imeshapambazuka.

discourses.source_txt: Bahati’s sense of time was always guided by passersby. She had become accustomed to hearing the movements of people going to work, to school, to the mosque, passenger airplanes, and the calls to prayer (p.20).
discourses.translated_txt: Hisia ya muda ya Bahati ilikuwa ikiendeshwa kila wakati na wapita njia. Alikuwa amezoea kusikia harakati za watu waendao kazini, shuleni, msikitini, ndege za abiria, na mwito wa sala (uk.20).

discourses.source_txt: The words emphasized in the above passage are used as personification, because in real life only a human being is capable of showing compassion toward another person or creature. Sleep is a state in which a person loses consciousness, as expressed in the Swahili saying, "sleep is half of death." However, in the above passage, sleep appears to have been given the ability to feel compassion, as if it were human.
discourses.translated_txt: Maneno yaliyosisitizwa katika kifungu hapo juu yanatumika kama ufananisho wa kutoa uhai kwa kitu kisicho na uhai, kwa sababu katika maisha halisi ni binadamu pekee anayeweza kuonyesha huruma kwa mtu mwingine au kiumbe. Usingizi ni hali ambayo mtu hupoteza fahamu, kama inavyoelezwa katika msemo wa Kiswahili, "usingizi ni nusu ya kifo." Hata hivyo, katika kifungu hicho hapo juu, usingizi unaonekana kupewa uwezo wa kuhisi huruma, kana kwamba ni binadamu.

discourses.source_txt:
5.1.5 The Use of Suspense in Kiu

Suspense is a literary technique used by authors of literary works to craft their works in such a way that they effectively convey their intended themes to the target audience.
discourses.translated_txt: Suto ni mbinu ya kifasihi inayotumiwa na waandishi wa kazi za fasihi kutunga kazi zao kwa namna ambayo zinawasilisha kwa ufanisi dhamira walizokusudia kwa hadhira lengwa.

discourses.source_txt: This is a technique of delaying the reader from obtaining the solution or the truth of the matter, and making them continue reading until they encounter a solution or some explanation that will provide the answer they intended to find (Senkoro, 2006).
discourses.translated_txt: Hii ni mbinu ya kuchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhisho au ukweli wa jambo fulani, na kumfanya aendelee kusoma hadi akumbane na suluhisho au maelezo fulani yatakayotoa jibu alilokusudia kulipata (Senkoro, 2006).

discourses.source_txt: The suspense technique is deliberately used by authors of literary works to give the reader or listener the desire to continue reading, especially when the work in question is lengthy enough to tire the reader. The length of the work will seem very short if there are suspenseful moments that captivate the reader.
discourses.translated_txt: Mbinu ya kusisimua hutumiwa makusudi na waandishi wa kazi za fasihi ili kumpa msomaji au msikilizaji hamu ya kuendelea kusoma, hasa pale kazi husika inapokuwa ndefu kiasi cha kumchosha msomaji. Urefu wa kazi utaonekana kuwa mfupi sana ikiwa kuna nyakati za kusisimua zinazomvutia msomaji.

discourses.source_txt:
Suspense is an ancient literary technique that is widely used in oral literature and even in written literature. Mohamed Suleiman, in his novel *Kiu*, has employed this technique in the way he begins narrating his story. For example:

That evening, he was stretched out on a reclining chair, his eyes fixed on the ceiling, counting the minutes. His desire was not great, and the anxiety of failure had robbed him of joy. If only what he wanted was within his grasp, he would seize it and quench his thirst.
discourses.translated_txt:
Msisimko ni mbinu ya zamani ya fasihi ambayo inatumika sana katika fasihi simulizi na hata katika fasihi andishi. Mohamed Suleiman, katika riwaya yake *Kiu*, ametumia mbinu hii katika namna anavyoanza kusimulia hadithi yake. Kwa mfano:

Jioni hiyo, alikuwa amelala kwenye kiti cha ku reclining, macho yake yamekazia kwenye dari, akihesabu dakika. Tamaa yake haikuwa kubwa, na wasiwasi wa kushindwa ulikuwa umeondoa furaha yake. Laiti kile alichotaka kingekuwa mikononi mwake, angekikamata na kutuliza kiu yake.

discourses.source_txt: If what he wanted could be bought with money, he would surely have scraped together every cent he had.
discourses.translated_txt: Kama kile alichokitaka kingeweza kununuliwa kwa pesa, angekuwa amekusanya kila senti aliyokuwa nayo.

discourses.source_txt: But the thing itself depended on the will of another person, someone with taste and pride.
discourses.translated_txt: Lakini kitu chenyewe kilitegemea mapenzi ya mtu mwingine, mtu mwenye ladha na fahari.

discourses.source_txt: So he had no choice but to ask and wait (pp. 01–02).
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa hiyo hakuwa na chaguo ila kuuliza na kusubiri (uk. 01–02).

discourses.source_txt: This passage contains a sense of anxiety, as there is something that makes Mwinyi uncomfortable and torments him despite being wealthy.
discourses.translated_txt: Dondoo hii ina hisia ya wasiwasi, kwani kuna kitu kinachomfanya Mwinyi ajisikie vibaya na kumtesa licha ya kuwa na utajiri.

discourses.source_txt:
This is not stated explicitly, but it is merely mentioned that if obtaining that thing required money, Mwinyi would provide it.  
“Stop joking, Iddi,” Mwinyi scolded him.
discourses.translated_txt:
Hili halijasemwa waziwazi, bali imetajwa tu kwamba kama kupata kitu hicho kungehitaji pesa, Mwinyi angekitoa.  
"Acha utani, Iddi," Mwinyi alimkemea.

discourses.source_txt: “Do you think a child like that could love an old man like me (p.05)?” In this passage, the tension built by the author on the first page of his novel begins to find answers on page five.
discourses.translated_txt: "Je, unafikiri mtoto kama huyo anaweza kumpenda mzee kama mimi (uk.05)?" Katika kifungu hiki, mvutano ulioumbwa na mwandishi kwenye ukurasa wa kwanza wa riwaya yake unaanza kupata majibu ukurasa wa tano.

discourses.source_txt: This is where the issue that troubles Mwinyi is mentioned, to the extent that he lacks peace despite all his great wealth.
discourses.translated_txt: Hapa ndipo tatizo linalomsumbua Mwinyi linapotajwa, kiasi kwamba hana amani licha ya utajiri wake mkubwa.

discourses.source_txt: That thing is none other than the love he had for a girl known by the name Bahati. Mwinyi was a man of sixty-two years, but he loved Bahati very much, even though she was a young girl who had not yet finished school.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitu hicho si kingine bali ni upendo aliokuwa nao kwa msichana anayeitwa Bahati. Mwinyi alikuwa mwanaume wa miaka sitini na miwili, lakini alipenda sana Bahati, ingawa alikuwa msichana mdogo ambaye bado hakuwa amemaliza shule.

discourses.source_txt: In this context, another tension arises: could Bahati agree to become the lover of an older man, just as Mwinyi did? This too creates suspense for the readers, who will be compelled to read further to find out what will happen regarding Mwinyi’s love for the young girl Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: Katika muktadha huu, mvutano mwingine unatokea: je, Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa mpenzi wa mwanaume mzee, kama vile Mwinyi alivyofanya? Hili pia linazua msisimko kwa wasomaji, ambao watalazimika kuendelea kusoma ili kujua nini kitatokea kuhusu mapenzi ya Mwinyi kwa msichana mdogo Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: The use of this technique of suspense has been employed with the aim of enhancing and developing the theme of love in the novel Kiu.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi ya mbinu hii ya wasiwasi yametumika kwa lengo la kuimarisha na kuendeleza dhamira ya mapenzi katika riwaya ya Kiu.

discourses.source_txt: This technique appears to be used repeatedly, as whenever the answer or solution to the initial suspense is found, another suspense is introduced (Mlacha, 1991).
discourses.translated_txt: Mbinu hii inaonekana kutumiwa mara kwa mara, kwani kila mara jibu au suluhisho la msisimko wa awali linapopatikana, msisimko mwingine unaanzishwa (Mlacha, 1991).

discourses.source_txt: For example, in the excerpt above we find the solution that what had been troubling Mwinyi Raha and causing him sleepless nights was his love for Bahati's daughter.
discourses.translated_txt: Kwa mfano, katika dondoo hapo juu tunapata suluhisho kwamba kilichokuwa kinamsumbua Mwinyi Raha na kumsababishia kukosa usingizi usiku ilikuwa ni mapenzi yake kwa binti wa Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: After realizing this, another anxiety has arisen as to whether such a young girl like Bahati could agree to be in a relationship with old Mwinyi, who could even be Bahati's father.
discourses.translated_txt: Baada ya kutambua hili, hofu nyingine imezuka kuhusu kama msichana mchanga kama Bahati anaweza kukubali kuwa kwenye uhusiano na Mwinyi mzee, ambaye hata angeweza kuwa baba yake Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Readers will continue reading until they find a solution, and after that, they will encounter another anxiety.
discourses.translated_txt: Wasomaji wataendelea kusoma hadi watakapopata suluhisho, na baada ya hapo, watakutana na wasiwasi mwingine.

discourses.source_txt: Conclusion The specific objective of this work was to analyze and describe the stylistic techniques used to construct social themes in the novel "Kiu" by Mohamed Suleiman. Accordingly, the findings include the use of stylistic techniques such as letters, expressions, metaphors, personification, and anxiety.
discourses.translated_txt: Hitimisho Lengo mahususi la kazi hii lilikuwa kuchambua na kuelezea mbinu za kisanaa zilizotumiwa kujenga dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya ya "Kiu" ya Mohamed Suleiman. Hivyo basi, matokeo yanajumuisha matumizi ya mbinu za kisanaa kama barua, misemo, tashihisi, ufananisho, na wasiwasi.

discourses.source_txt: The research findings show that the novel 'Kiu' by Mohamed Suleiman is rich in stylistic techniques, but in this study we have focused only on the use of the letter-writing technique, sayings, metaphor, anxiety, and suspense. The main reason for selecting these five techniques is that they adequately meet the objectives of this research.
discourses.translated_txt: Matokeo ya utafiti yanaonyesha kuwa riwaya ya 'Kiu' ya Mohamed Suleiman imejaa mbinu za kisanaa, lakini katika utafiti huu tumejikita tu kwenye matumizi ya mbinu ya uandishi wa barua, methali, sitiari, wasiwasi, na msisimko. Sababu kuu ya kuchagua mbinu hizi tano ni kwamba zinakidhi ipasavyo malengo ya utafiti huu.

discourses.source_txt: The use of the letter-writing technique was employed with the aim of developing and advancing the theme of love, in which Bahati wanted to know if Iddi truly loved her. Bahati wrote a letter to inform Iddi that she was now genuinely in love with Mwinyi and asked Iddi not to bother her, as they were now planning their wedding. This letter tormented Iddi to the point where he did not know what to do, because he had already realized that all the plans he had made with Bahati were now ruined. However, the content of the letter was intended to test whether Iddi truly loved Bahati.
discourses.translated_txt: Matumizi ya mbinu ya kuandika barua yalitumiwa kwa lengo la kuendeleza na kukuza dhamira ya mapenzi, ambapo Bahati alitaka kujua kama Iddi kweli anampenda. Bahati aliandika barua kumjulisha Iddi kwamba sasa anampenda Mwinyi kwa dhati na akamwomba Iddi amwache, kwani sasa walikuwa wanapanga harusi yao. Barua hii ilimsumbua Iddi hadi akashindwa kujua la kufanya, kwa sababu tayari aligundua kwamba mipango yote aliyokuwa amefanya na Bahati sasa imeharibika. Hata hivyo, yaliyomo kwenye barua hiyo yalilenga kujaribu kama Iddi kweli anampenda Bahati.

discourses.source_txt: Bahati knew that Iddi loved her because he became upset after reading the letter she had sent him.
discourses.translated_txt: Bahati alijua kwamba Iddi alimpenda kwa sababu alikasirika baada ya kusoma barua aliyomtumia.

discourses.source_txt: It turned out that Iddi was not upset because he really loved Bahati; rather, he saw clearly
discourses.translated_txt: Ilibainika kuwa Iddi hakuwa amekasirika kwa sababu alimpenda sana Bahati; bali, aliona wazi kabisa

discourses.source_txt: Some Stylistic Techniques in Swahili Novels: "The Novel Kiu by Mohamed Suleiman as an Example" Ali.
discourses.translated_txt: Baadhi ya mbinu za kisanii katika riwaya za Kiswahili: "Riwaya ya Kiu ya Mohamed Suleiman kama Mfano" na Ali.

discourses.source_txt: Mwinyi’s plans to gain wealth through Bahati had become nothing more than an unattainable dream.
discourses.translated_txt: Mipango ya Mwinyi ya kupata utajiri kupitia Bahati ilikuwa imebaki kuwa ndoto isiyoweza kufikiwa.

discourses.source_txt: Suspense is another artistic technique that has been used to highlight social themes in Mohamed Suleiman's novel Kiu. This technique has been employed in the arrangement of plots and events, where right from the beginning the novel starts with suspense.
discourses.translated_txt: Msisimko ni mbinu nyingine ya kisanii iliyotumika kuangazia mada za kijamii katika riwaya ya Mohamed Suleiman, Kiu. Mbinu hii imetumika katika upangaji wa njama na matukio, ambapo tangu mwanzo riwaya inaanza kwa msisimko.

discourses.source_txt: The situation of delaying the reader from finding the solution to what is being described in the novel creates in the reader a desire to read more, as they will want to continue reading in order to reach the conclusion of the event. For example, at the beginning of the novel, it is described that Mwinyi lives in hardship and lacks happiness despite being a wealthy person.
discourses.translated_txt: Hali ya kumchelewesha msomaji kupata suluhisho la kile kinachoelezewa katika riwaya humfanya msomaji atamani kusoma zaidi, kwani atataka kuendelea kusoma ili afikie hitimisho la tukio. Kwa mfano, mwanzoni mwa riwaya, inaelezwa kuwa Mwinyi anaishi kwenye matatizo na anakosa furaha licha ya kuwa mtu tajiri.

discourses.source_txt: The thing that is said to be depriving Mwinyi of happiness is his love for Bahati, something he believes cannot succeed because he is an old man and Bahati is a young woman.
discourses.translated_txt: Kitu kinachosemekana kinamnyima Mwinyi furaha ni upendo wake kwa Bahati, jambo ambalo anaamini haliwezi kufanikiwa kwa sababu yeye ni mzee na Bahati ni mwanamke mchanga.

discourses.source_txt: Other stylistic techniques used to develop social themes in the novel "Kiu" include proverbs, metaphors, and personification. These literary techniques have been employed to emphasize various issues related to social themes in the novel "Kiu."
discourses.translated_txt: Mbinu nyingine za kisanii zilizotumika kuendeleza dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya "Kiu" ni pamoja na nahau, methali, na uchanganuzi wa mtu. Mbinu hizi za fasihi zimetumika kusisitiza masuala mbalimbali yanayohusiana na dhamira za kijamii katika riwaya "Kiu."
